title: Independent Variation Principle
text:
The Independent Variation Principle (IVP) is a theory of software architecture and, more broadly, of how structured systems are organized around the sources of change that act upon them.
This site is the working home for the IVP theory, its hypotheses, its conclusions, and the ongoing development tracked in this repository and its referenced literature.



Development Topics Inventory — the complete list of every topic, theory, and development thread related to IVP. This is the map of the site.

title: IVP Development Topics — Complete Inventory
text:
Purpose: Exhaustive inventory of every topic, theory, and development thread related to the Independent Variation Principle (IVP) and its broader theory, as present in this project (src/, meta/) and in the literature submodules (literature/PIV, literature/PIV-Article, literature/PIV-Formalization-ICSA2026).
Use: This list drives the navigation structure of the static IVP web site. Each topic is a candidate page, section, or category. The list is complete as of 2026-08-27.



The Change Management Hypothesis (CMH) is the normative postulate that structure is optimal when it minimizes lifetime coordination cost around change drivers. IVP is derived from CMH.

CMH as the surviving foundation among competing modularization-theory alternatives (survey of six alternatives).
CMH applied to enterprise-architecture structuring (nine alternative foundations evaluated; CMH unique).
Graph-theoretic proof that CMH prescribes exactly four cost-optimal conditions (bipartite incidence graphs, gamma-equality).
CMH as a normative postulate, not an empirical hypothesis (historical classification).
The two-stage adoption structure of CMH (motivational introduction → formal development).
Volume-0: “The Change Management Hypothesis: Foundations of Modularization Theory” — full CMH treatment across software, organizations, business processes.
Business formulation of CMH: structure is optimal when it minimizes lifetime coordination cost around change drivers (enterprise/business application).
CMH derivation chain: system tuple, cost factorization, model-fidelity premise, structural exhaustion (M1–M4), CMH-compatible cost-model class, four conditions.
Brooks’s Law derived as a corollary of CMH.
The coordination-cost derivation of IVP from CMH (the “coordination anchor”).





The formal apparatus of IVP: system tuple, change drivers, elements, modules, knowledge, coupling, and the four axioms.

Software system tuple S = (F, κ_F, E, 𝒦, C, Γ) — functional purpose, relevant causal domain knowledge, elements, coupling relation, change-driver set, assignment.
Knowledge structure — Knowledge, Domain Knowledge, Causal Domain Knowledge, Relevant Causal Domain Knowledge, Knowledge Slices (κ_F = ⊔ᵢ κ_γᵢ).
Change drivers γ ∈ C — discrete sources of variation; coupling dimension = leaf-level driver.
Change-driver assignment Γ: E → 𝒫(C); change-driver independence γᵢ ⊥ γⱼ; causal dependence between drivers γⱼ ⇝ γᵢ.
Change-driver refinement γ ▷ {γ₁,…,γₙ} — domain decomposition.
Elements e ∈ E — pure, composite, irreducible-composite (translation/adapter, combination), reducible-composite.
Modules M ⊆ E and Modularization ℳ (partition of E); module driver set Γ(M) = ⋃_{e∈M} Γ(e).
Domain — coherent region of causal knowledge; more precise than DDD’s “domain.”
Variation dependence — Γ-equivalence classes; the equivalence relation forming the IVP-compliant partition.
The four IVP axioms — IVP-1 (Element Admissibility), IVP-2 (Change-Driver Assignment), IVP-3 (Unit Purity/Separation), IVP-4 (Unit Completeness/Unification); the biconditional e₁~e₂ ⟺ Γ(e₁)=Γ(e₂).
Partition Theorem — IVP-compliance gives a unique (up to coarsening) optimal partition.
Knowledge Theorem — cohesion ⟺ knowledge embodiment; maximal cohesion (purity+completeness) ⟺ complete+pure formalization of domain knowledge.
Knowledge embodiment / pure knowledge / complete knowledge / maximal knowledge embodiment.
Causal cohesion — Γ-equivalence as modularization principle; causal cohesion metric (purity, completeness).
Coupling — the coupling relation 𝒦, coupling instances, propagation mechanisms (structural/temporal/concurrency/semantic/platform), coupling dimensions.
Coupling decomposition — necessary + spurious + accidental; structural vs causal dependencies.
Causal coupling / cohesion primacy — coupling is a consequence of cohesion, not an independent trade-off.
The six-step IVP application process — pre-design, design, validation.
Driver omission theory — omitting a driver coarsens the optimal partition; remediation cost; orthogonality vs entanglement; triage.
Refactoring convergence theorem — change-driver-directed moves strictly decrease distance to the Γ-optimal partition.
Multi-dimensional coupling — six coupling dimensions; Γ-partition eliminates accidental coupling in all at once.
Objects as modules — IVP criterion for what makes a correct object at object granularity.
Domain–infrastructure boundary — as a structural property of the driver set.
Acyclicity / dependency cycles — three graphs, types of knowledge cycles, breaking fundamental cycles.





Further formal results and refinements built on the core theory.

Quality Meta-Theorem — quality attributes as change drivers; locality condition.
Cohesion monotonicity (extended theorem).
Change-driver hierarchies (extended theorem).
Necessary vs accidental impurity — multi-driver elements; adapters are necessarily impure.
Multi-dimensional architecture spaces.
Variation velocity.
Meta-theorem stability under driver evolution.
Partition property / partition constraints — when a valid partition exists; the non-existence theorem; seven regimes of driver completeness; semantic unification under incomplete drivers.
Compositional Γ — transparent vs coupled composition; multi-element scale; operadic structure.
Driver overlap algebra — driver-overlap graph, connected components, treewidth bounds.
Pathway theory — pathway-template theorem, construct-vocabulary pathways, Γ^(2), Γ_floor.
Floor characterization & monotonicity — language-bounded irreducible drivers.
Substitution cost decomposition — Δ + δ_ret + δ_dom; telescoping identity.
Cross-element pathway externality / system-Pareto improvement.
Four conditions — admissibility, element form, separation, unification (CMH optimum).
Structural impossibility — no structural measurement can decide element placement.
Scalar-verdict impossibility — no scalar decides placement by measuring.
Metric floor — information-theoretic floor on structural metrics.
Cycle analysis (shared definitions).
Interface ownership — client-driven, provider-driven, shared-governance evolution.
Dependency concepts — abstraction, contract, interface, indirection, Γ-equivalence, structural dependency, variation dependence.
Knowledge management framing (KM) — software as crystallized knowledge.
Modularity impedance (remarks).
Cost models — total maintenance cost decomposition (access, reading, disturbance, cognitive overhead, domain-fixed); alternative cost anchors.
Entropy anchor — Boltzmann entropy as a fourth normative anchor; IVP minimizes entropy growth; entropy as falsifiable prediction.
Categorical structure of construct substitution — functors, limits, coherence diagrams.
Sheaf of construct choices — cohomological obstruction H¹.
Topology/uniform structure on construct vocabularies — Cauchy completions, limit constructs.
Galois connection between pathway selection and Γ-projection.
Operadic structure of compositional Γ — strict vs lax operad morphisms.
Model-theoretic floor via ultralimits — language-essential floor.
Profunctor view of specification-implementation.
Group actions on construct vocabularies — orbits, symmetry analysis.
Homotopy of refactoring paths — π₁, higher homotopy.
Spectral decomposition of the substitution operator (speculative).
Information-theoretic floor bound — Kolmogorov complexity bound on floor drivers.
Axiom independence — IVP-1/2/3/4 mutually independent (outstanding author task).

Multi-representation situations — multi-algorithm, format, persistence (A1–A3).

Hierarchy & abstraction — stability/abstraction hierarchies, microservices.
Independence situations — interface/initialization/pluggable (E1–E3).
Persistent invariants, versioning, caching, batch processing (F/G situations).
Fundamental principles — Separation of Concerns, Information Hiding, Cohesion & Coupling as IVP special cases.
SOLID principles — all five derived from IVP (complete bidirectional proofs).
Package principles — all six (CCP, CRP, REP, ADP, SDP, SAP).
Robert Martin synthesis — what SOLID gets right and where it fails.
Architectural styles — Layered, Hexagonal (ports & adapters), Clean Architecture, Modern patterns (microservices, event-driven, CQRS).
Domain-Driven Design — Strategic DDD (bounded contexts, context maps), Tactical DDD (aggregates, entities, value objects).
Code quality — DRY, YAGNI, KISS, Law of Demeter.
Functional programming — purity, immutability via IVP.

Additional principles — security, performance, i18n.

Invariants, versioning, performance (A1–G2).
Principle index / contrapositive analysis / principle selection guide / automated checking (Volume 2 appendices).





Pointed results about individual principles, mostly negative or corrective. These are the “SRP is false”-style results.

SRP is false — SRP as Martin states it fails; the adapter pattern is a counterexample; cardinality + people-grounding fail.
SRP vocabulary problem — why three decades of reformulations failed (vocabulary hid the cardinality error).
SRP–CCP–ISP triangle — the three collapse into one partitioning mechanism.
CCP is not a principle — “change together” admits two readings, only one survives.
ISP is DIP — ISP is a conditional corollary of DIP applied per client; gated by interface-evolution origin.
ISP is DIP (packaging) — where client-owned interfaces physically live.
ISP is DIP (with IVP) — formal IVP proof.
DIP is a theorem of IVP — from independent variation, decisional dependency, contract-feasibility.
DIP domain knowledge — interfaces embody domain knowledge vs. form overhead.
SDP causal stability — Stable Dependencies derived causally (vs. Martin’s metric-only stability).
What remains of SOLID — deconstruction; what conditionally survives (LSP/OCP dismissed).
SRP formalization (shared definitions).
Martin heuristics note — SOLID/package rules are informal heuristics, not formal principles.
GRASP deconstructed — nine patterns reduce to an unresolved Low-Coupling/High-Cohesion tension with no decision procedure.
Co-change impossibility — co-change (MSR) cannot recover any partitioning rule; abductive candidate generation only.
Co-change driver structure — the impossibility instantiated for Γ.
Co-change practitioner guide — the surviving abductive role.





The cohesion series develops cohesion from first principles and its causal (IVP) form. (Full paper series in src/main/typst/cohesion/.)

cohesion-1-survey — survey of 24 cohesion metrics; all measure structural coupling, not principled cohesion.
cohesion-2-nature — cohesion as correctness relative to a partitioning rule; (purity, completeness) pair; knowledge-embodiment theorem; the cohesion schema.
cohesion-3-graded-embodiment — monotonic equivalence at all intermediate cohesion levels.
cohesion-4-causal — causal cohesion metric H_causal under Γ-equivalence.
cohesion-5-optimal — four conditions necessary and exhaustive; select the unique Γ-partition.
cohesion-6-maintenance — change-propagation cost = total maintenance cost; cognitive overhead as new dimension.
cohesion-7-ivp — synthesis into IVP; premises and boundary conditions.
cohesion-8-structural-blindness — no structural measurement can decide placement.
cohesion-9-scalar-verdict — no scalar decides placement by measuring.
cohesion-10-composition — combining modularisation principles.
cohesion-11-principles-survey — existing practice survey; none satisfies all four conditions.
cohesion-12-principle-candidates — formal framework candidates (graph partitioning, info bottleneck, MDL, spectral, causal, coalgebraic).
cohesion-13-cost-models — alternative cost anchors.
cohesion-14-entropy — Boltzmann entropy as fourth normative anchor.
cohesion-15-entropy-prediction — entropy-based falsifiable prediction about real codebases.





The coupling series develops coupling from first principles (shared-resource coupling) and its relation to IVP. (Full paper series in src/main/typst/coupling/.)

coupling-1-survey — five-decade survey; the unification gap.
coupling-2-nature — coupling = access to a shared resource; ternary (element, resource, element); visibility principle.
coupling-3-derivation — grouping by identical resource-access minimizes accidental coupling; derives Γ from R.
coupling-4-primacy-decomposition — coupling is a consequence of cohesion; eight-category decomposition; coupling floor.
coupling-5-completeness — decomposition under the IVP partition; residual coupling catalog.
coupling-6-metric-floor — information-theoretic floor for structural metrics.
coupling-7-activation — design decisions as operators on the concern set.
coupling-8-reconciliation — every classical coupling level read as shared-resource coupling.
coupling-9-transitive-counting — transitive coupling graphs are linear in resource count.
coupling-10-transitive-lattice — full resource-set partition is the meet of per-dimension partitions.

title: IVP Development Topics — Complete Inventory
text:
The Change Management Hypothesis (CMH) is the normative postulate that structure is optimal when it minimizes lifetime coordination cost around change drivers. IVP is derived from CMH.

CMH as the surviving foundation among competing modularization-theory alternatives (survey of six alternatives).
CMH applied to enterprise-architecture structuring (nine alternative foundations evaluated; CMH unique).
Graph-theoretic proof that CMH prescribes exactly four cost-optimal conditions (bipartite incidence graphs, gamma-equality).
CMH as a normative postulate, not an empirical hypothesis (historical classification).
The two-stage adoption structure of CMH (motivational introduction → formal development).
Volume-0: “The Change Management Hypothesis: Foundations of Modularization Theory” — full CMH treatment across software, organizations, business processes.
Business formulation of CMH: structure is optimal when it minimizes lifetime coordination cost around change drivers (enterprise/business application).
CMH derivation chain: system tuple, cost factorization, model-fidelity premise, structural exhaustion (M1–M4), CMH-compatible cost-model class, four conditions.
Brooks’s Law derived as a corollary of CMH.
The coordination-cost derivation of IVP from CMH (the “coordination anchor”).

title: IVP Development Topics — Complete Inventory
text:
The formal apparatus of IVP: system tuple, change drivers, elements, modules, knowledge, coupling, and the four axioms.

Software system tuple S = (F, κ_F, E, 𝒦, C, Γ) — functional purpose, relevant causal domain knowledge, elements, coupling relation, change-driver set, assignment.
Knowledge structure — Knowledge, Domain Knowledge, Causal Domain Knowledge, Relevant Causal Domain Knowledge, Knowledge Slices (κ_F = ⊔ᵢ κ_γᵢ).
Change drivers γ ∈ C — discrete sources of variation; coupling dimension = leaf-level driver.
Change-driver assignment Γ: E → 𝒫(C); change-driver independence γᵢ ⊥ γⱼ; causal dependence between drivers γⱼ ⇝ γᵢ.
Change-driver refinement γ ▷ {γ₁,…,γₙ} — domain decomposition.
Elements e ∈ E — pure, composite, irreducible-composite (translation/adapter, combination), reducible-composite.
Modules M ⊆ E and Modularization ℳ (partition of E); module driver set Γ(M) = ⋃_{e∈M} Γ(e).
Domain — coherent region of causal knowledge; more precise than DDD’s “domain.”
Variation dependence — Γ-equivalence classes; the equivalence relation forming the IVP-compliant partition.
The four IVP axioms — IVP-1 (Element Admissibility), IVP-2 (Change-Driver Assignment), IVP-3 (Unit Purity/Separation), IVP-4 (Unit Completeness/Unification); the biconditional e₁~e₂ ⟺ Γ(e₁)=Γ(e₂).
Partition Theorem — IVP-compliance gives a unique (up to coarsening) optimal partition.
Knowledge Theorem — cohesion ⟺ knowledge embodiment; maximal cohesion (purity+completeness) ⟺ complete+pure formalization of domain knowledge.
Knowledge embodiment / pure knowledge / complete knowledge / maximal knowledge embodiment.
Causal cohesion — Γ-equivalence as modularization principle; causal cohesion metric (purity, completeness).
Coupling — the coupling relation 𝒦, coupling instances, propagation mechanisms (structural/temporal/concurrency/semantic/platform), coupling dimensions.
Coupling decomposition — necessary + spurious + accidental; structural vs causal dependencies.
Causal coupling / cohesion primacy — coupling is a consequence of cohesion, not an independent trade-off.
The six-step IVP application process — pre-design, design, validation.
Driver omission theory — omitting a driver coarsens the optimal partition; remediation cost; orthogonality vs entanglement; triage.
Refactoring convergence theorem — change-driver-directed moves strictly decrease distance to the Γ-optimal partition.
Multi-dimensional coupling — six coupling dimensions; Γ-partition eliminates accidental coupling in all at once.
Objects as modules — IVP criterion for what makes a correct object at object granularity.
Domain–infrastructure boundary — as a structural property of the driver set.
Acyclicity / dependency cycles — three graphs, types of knowledge cycles, breaking fundamental cycles.

title: IVP Development Topics — Complete Inventory
text:
Pointed results about individual principles, mostly negative or corrective. These are the “SRP is false”-style results.

SRP is false — SRP as Martin states it fails; the adapter pattern is a counterexample; cardinality + people-grounding fail.
SRP vocabulary problem — why three decades of reformulations failed (vocabulary hid the cardinality error).
SRP–CCP–ISP triangle — the three collapse into one partitioning mechanism.
CCP is not a principle — “change together” admits two readings, only one survives.
ISP is DIP — ISP is a conditional corollary of DIP applied per client; gated by interface-evolution origin.
ISP is DIP (packaging) — where client-owned interfaces physically live.
ISP is DIP (with IVP) — formal IVP proof.
DIP is a theorem of IVP — from independent variation, decisional dependency, contract-feasibility.
DIP domain knowledge — interfaces embody domain knowledge vs. form overhead.

SRP formalization (shared definitions).

Co-change impossibility — co-change (MSR) cannot recover any partitioning rule; abductive candidate generation only.
Co-change driver structure — the impossibility instantiated for Γ.
Co-change practitioner guide — the surviving abductive role.

title: IVP Development Topics — Complete Inventory
text:
These threads recur across many parts and may deserve top-level navigation:

Foundations — CMH, system tuple, axioms, knowledge, domains.
Formal theory — theorems, proofs, partition, cohesion, coupling.
Unification — classical principles derived from IVP.
Corrective results — “SRP is false,” co-change impossibility, structural blindness.
Applications — engineering practices, domains, patterns.
Organizational — Conway, enterprise architecture, teams.
GTSO — the general theory, non-software domains.
Mathematical depth — Volume 5 frameworks.
Research frontier — open questions, entropy prediction, research ideas.
Series/books — the five volumes and their companions.
